paragraphs: Peterborough City Council has run its own not-for-profit fostering service since 1 November 2023, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers who live in and around the city. With the council you look after Peterborough's own children, and it aims to keep them close to their birth families; an agency assesses, trains and supervises you itself and offers homes to children that councils ask it to place.

The service's statement of purpose recorded 74 approved foster carers in March 2024, counting respite, link and family-and-friends carers and 134 children living in its foster homes. The council says it most needs homes that can keep brothers and sisters together, carers for children over 10 and teenagers, homes for disabled children and those with complex health or emotional needs, and families for children who need to stay long term. Its sufficiency statement for 2025 to 2029, approved by the cabinet in November 2025, aims for as many children in care as possible to live locally where that is right for them, and after a monitoring visit in July 2025 Ofsted noted that the council's investment had brought an increase in local foster carers.

You need to be over 21 with a spare bedroom. You can be retired, rent your home or be out of work, nobody is too old, and for most kinds of fostering a job is no barrier, though you will need some experience of children. The route runs from enquiry and a home visit through a four-day course and an assessment to a fostering panel, normally four to six months in all.

The council offers emergency care for up to 72 hours, time-limited care for up to two years, long-term fostering, respite, parent and baby care and kinship care. Its Link scheme gives disabled children living at home short breaks, from one or two nights a month up to 208 nights a year, and supported lodgings hosts for 16 to 21 year olds are paid £250 a week. Carers have an experienced carer as a mentor, a supervising social worker, free Fostering Network membership, an employee assistance service and family membership of the city's Vivacity leisure centres, with fees on top of the child's allowance that rise with skills and experience. A Mockingbird hub started in November 2025 links nine fostering families and eighteen children, and Anglian Water, Nene Park Trust and Meridian Trust have joined the council's Foster Friendly scheme, which usually gives staff who foster up to five extra days' leave a year.
We have no Peterborough pay page yet, so ask the council and two or three services above for current rates. The Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire pages list more services nearby.
